chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa from al-Husayn b. Sayf from Sallam b. Ghanim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said:

Whoever says "there is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illallah) one hundred times when he goes to his bed, Allah builds a house for him in Paradise. And whoever seeks forgiveness (istighfar) one hundred times when he goes to his bed, his sins will fall away just as the leaves of a tree fall.

key_terms.استغفر: To seek forgiveness from Allah (istighfar), a key devotional practice in Islam
key_terms.تحاتت: To fall away or erode gradually, used here as a vivid metaphor for the erasure of sins
key_terms.فراش: Bed or sleeping place, indicating this is a bedtime devotional practice
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: The declaration of divine unity (tahlil), the most fundamental statement of Islamic monotheism

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of saying la ilaha illallah and seeking forgiveness before sleeping according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), narrated in a gathering in Muharram 368 AH, teaches two bedtime devotional practices: reciting the tahlil (la ilaha illallah) one hundred times earns a house in Paradise, and seeking forgiveness (istighfar) one hundred times causes sins to fall away like leaves from a tree. These practices reflect the importance of concluding each day with remembrance of God and repentance.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to me. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from al-Husayn b. Sayf from Salam b. Ghanim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

Whoever says “there is no god but Allah (la ilaha illallah)” one hundred times when he goes to his bed, Allah builds a house for him in Paradise. Whoever repents (istighfar) one hundred times when he goes to his bed, his sins will erode just as the leaves of a tree fall.
